channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Plano de governo diz que Lula é antissistema: 'Verdadeiro novo'
item.description: The PT submitted Lula's government plan to the Electoral Justice as part of the candidate registration, comprising 13 chapters across 84 pages. The document is portrayed as a 'treasury of promises' for a fourth term, yet also as a 'challenge to logic' when evaluated as campaign material. The article's headline frames Lula as an 'anti-system' figure and 'the true new'.

item.title: A sabatina de Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos, candidate from the Missão party, was the first to be interviewed by journalists Natuza Nery and Andréia Sadi on GloboNews in the podcast 'O Assunto'. The discussion covered key issues of the 2026 presidential campaign.

item.title: Atentados marcam 1º dia de governo de Espriella na Colômbia
item.description: On the first day of President Abelardo De la Espriella's government in Colombia, explosive attacks attributed to armed groups linked to Iván Mordisco left one police officer dead and two security guards injured. The attacks occurred on the Pan-American Highway in Mondomo (Cauca) and at a police station in Cesar, immediately testing the new president's promise to harden security policy. The government labeled the attacks as terrorism and launched operations to apprehend those responsible.

item.title: PT e PL aliam apoios táticos e chapas puras nos estados por palanque nacional
item.description: PT and PL established tactical alliances with center-party candidates in states while maintaining pure slates to strengthen the national contest between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. Party conventions concluded with strategies focused on state-level slates to support the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Tarcísio e Haddad voltam a se enfrentar pelo Governo de SP em debate na Band
item.description: Former minister Fernando Haddad (PT) and Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) are set to face off again in a Band debate, four years after their last electoral encounter, for the São Paulo gubernatorial race. The debate will take place this Sunday (9) at 8 p.m., featuring only the two candidates on stage, with no other contenders present.

item.title: Zema declara R$ 178,7 milhões em bens ao TSE; Girão informa R$ 34,1 milhões
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential candidate, declared R$178.7 million in assets to the TSE, a 37.7% increase from 2022, driven by higher equity stakes and investment restructuring. His running mate, Eduardo Girão, reported R$34.1 million in assets, a 6.3% decrease from R$36.3 million declared in 2018. Both figures are part of the ticket's registration filing submitted to the TSE on Friday (7).

item.title: Renan Santos chama Moro de ‘rato’; senador rebate: ‘ofensas imaturas para lacrar na internet’
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos (Mission Party) insulted Senator Sergio Moro, calling him a 'rat', 'weak', and 'defeated' at a Paraná congress. Moro responded by refusing to engage with 'immature insults from those seeking online clout' and emphasized his Lava-Jato record, including imprisoning Lula and isolating PCC leaders. Moro leads the Paraná gubernatorial race by up to 21 points in polls.

item.title: A bronca de juízes do STF com o ministro da Justiça
item.description: STF judges complained to President Lula about the alleged apathy of Justice Minister Wellington Lima e Silva regarding the Federal Police, amid investigations targeting Lulinha and suspicions of influence peddling. Tensions rose due to PF leaks involving Minister Toffoli and the Master case, plus allegations of parallel police activity in the office of Minister André Mendonça, who seeks to be removed from the rapporteurship of inquiries against the president’s son. The situation unfolds less than two months before the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election.

item.title: "Corrupto e criminoso": Milei republica publicação com críticas a Lula
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei reposted social media criticisms of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, labeling him 'corrupt and criminal' and accusing him of enabling communist dictatorships. The posts came four days after Brazil downgraded diplomatic relations with Argentina, in response to Milei’s public attacks on Lula and Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Risco de André Mendonça é repetir Sérgio Moro ou Alexandre de Moraes
item.description: André Mendonça, STF minister appointed by Bolsonaro, risks repeating the mistakes of Sérgio Moro and Alexandre de Moraes by concentrating power and acting authoritatively in high-impact investigations such as Banco Master and INSS, despite initially demonstrating sound judgment. His stance is threatened by political polarization and pressures from his patrons — Bolsonaro and Lula — mediated through figures like Andrei Rodrigues of the Federal Police, undermining his independence. The text warns that fleeting power may lead him to the same downfall as his predecessors.

item.title: Tarcísio declara patrimônio menor que em 2022
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas declared a net worth of R$ 2,696 million to the Electoral Justice when registering his 2026 re-election bid, which is lower than the R$ 2,342 million he reported in 2022. Adjusted for inflation, the 2022 figure equals R$ 2,794 million, indicating a real decline of 3.5% in declared assets. Most of his holdings are in real estate and investments.

item.title: Novo aciona TSE contra chapa Lula-Alckmin por suposto abuso de poder
item.description: The Novo Party filed a Judicial Electoral Investigation Action (AIJE) with the TSE against the Lula-Alckmin ticket for alleged economic power abuse and improper use of media during the 2025 Carnival, claiming the Acadêmicos de Niterói parade honoring Lula was an illegal 'electoral show' funded by public resources. The suit seeks to annul the candidates' registrations and declare them ineligible for eight years. Lula attended the parade and interacted with the school, which placed last and was relegated to the Série Ouro for 2027.

item.title: Novo pede cassação de Lula e Alckmin por suposto abuso de poder econômico em desfile de carnaval
item.description: The Novo Party filed an AIJE at the TSE seeking the cancellation of Lula and Alckmin’s candidacies, alleging economic power abuse and improper use of media through a Carnival parade funded with R$9.65 million in public money. The party claims the parade, honoring Lula, served as electoral propaganda, citing public funding from multiple government levels, televised broadcasts, and references to political opponents and Bolsonaro’s family.

item.title: Tesouraço de Flávio fica entre a vassourinha de Jânio e a motosserra de Milei
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro wore a scissors-shaped lapel pin as a symbol of his proposed 'tesouraço' — a drastic cut in public spending, taxes, and bureaucracy. The imagery evokes Jânio Quadros's 'little broom' and Javier Milei's 'chainsaw,' reinforcing a rhetoric of aggressive state reduction. The gesture suggests a potential campaign strategy centered on radical fiscal austerity for the 2026 elections.

item.title: O time de conselheiros econômicos de Lula que contrapõe o PT ao seu governo
item.description: Lula's economic advisory team, including Dario Durigan, Bruno Moretti, Edinho Silva, Aloizio Mercadante, and José Sergio Gabrielli, has been working to solidify the president's economic platform, countering perceptions of heterodoxy and emphasizing continuity with current fiscal policies, such as the 17.9 billion reais budget block to comply with the fiscal framework. While acknowledging the need for fiscal tightening per market views, the advisors argue that government measures are appropriate and reject the term 'adjustment' in the campaign platform, which seeks only to formalize Lula's candidacy. The official projection of a 10.8 billion reais primary surplus relies on accounting exclusions; without them, the deficit would be 52 billion reais.

item.title: Novo aciona TSE pela cassação da chapa Lula-Alckmin
item.description: The Novo party filed a lawsuit with the TSE seeking the annulment of the Lula-Alckmin ticket and declaring both candidates ineligible for eight years, citing the Acadêmicos de Niterói samba school parade during Carnival as grounds. The action was filed on Saturday, the 8th, aiming to block their re-election. The original post appeared on O Antagonista.

item.title: Renan Santos declara R$ 795 mil em bens ao TSE; vice informa R$ 1,6 milhão
item.description: Renan Santos, pré-candidate of the Missão party for President of Brazil, declared R$ 795,000 in assets to the TSE, while his running mate, Aroldo Medina, reported R$ 1.6 million, totaling R$ 2.4 million in declared wealth. The candidacy registration was submitted on Friday (7) and is under review by the TSE, within the legal deadline of August 15. Renan listed four assets, including 'other credits and linked savings' (R$ 300,000) and assets related to self-employment (R$ 275,000), without specifying origins or institutions.

item.title: Como o caso Master influencia o voto dos eleitores? Veja o que diz pesquisa
item.description: A poll by Indexa Pesquisas shows 38% of voters are less likely to support candidates with political or personal ties to those investigated in the Banco Master case, while 35% see no difference and 3% are more inclined. The scandal, involving fraud and attempts by banker Daniel Vorcaro to shield himself via congressional lobbying, ex-minister hires, and appeals to STF and TCU officials, has the weakest impact in the Southeast and Northeast and the strongest in the South, where voters are split on its influence. Non-Bolsonarist right-wing voters are most likely to say it doesn’t affect their vote (41%), while Bolsonarist voters show the highest lack of awareness (20%).

item.title: A questão de classe de reacionários sem classe. Elites, rezem por Lula
item.description: The author criticizes the far-right's reaction to Lula's political strategy, arguing that the president acted correctly by making an alliance between bolsonarism and the Centrón unviable — it is the opposition's duty to attract allies, not the government's to ease their failure. He contends that Brazil's current power model favors the Executive through mechanisms like the Secret Budget and amendments, rendering Congress irrelevant and turning politics into a profitable enterprise for elites and lobbies, while Lula remains the only president capable of building ideologically coherent alliances across ten elections.

item.title: Bens de Lula caem 35% e os de Alckmin sobem mais de 200% em quatro anos
item.description: President Lula's declared assets fell by 35.67% over four years, dropping from 7.4 million to 4.7 million Brazilian reais, largely due to reduced private pension plans. Vice President Alckmin saw a 227.3% increase in declared assets, rising from about 1 million to nearly 3.3 million reais, driven by pension plans and financial investments. Other mentioned candidates include Romeu Zema, with 178.7 million reais in assets, and Renan Santos, with 759,000 reais.

item.title: Lula declara ao TSE patrimônio de R$ 4,7 milhões, valor 35% menor do que em 2022
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) declared a net worth of R$ 4.77 million to the TSE in his reelection bid, 35% lower than the R$ 7.42 million declared in 2022. The disclosure was filed on Saturday, March 8, as part of his candidacy registration with the Superior Electoral Court.

item.title: Lula reclama de exigências dos bancos para liberar financiamento do Move Brasil
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the requirements imposed by banks to release financing under the Move Brazil program, which supports app-based drivers, taxi drivers, and delivery workers in purchasing vehicles. He argued that the financial institutions' conditions hinder access to credit for these professionals.

item.title: A nova pesquisa presidencial da Quaest
item.description: Quaest is conducting its ninth presidential poll of 2026, interviewing 2,004 Brazilians in person from March 10 to 13, with results to be released on March 14. This is the first poll in a series commissioned by the Globo group (O GLOBO and TV Globo), with full access restricted to subscribers who register via the article link.

item.title: Moro diz que Valdemar 'já pagou' pelos erros 'no passado' e defende aliança com Bolsonaros após 'divergência séria'
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro (PL), candidate for governor of Paraná, defended the alliance with the Liberal Party and downplayed investigations against Valdemar Costa Neto, stating he 'already paid for past mistakes'. He accused the Lula government of interfering with the Federal Police and investigations against the president's son, Fábio Luís, and reaffirmed his support for Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 presidential bid.

item.title: Lula declara R$ 4,8 milhões em bens ao TSE; Alckmin informa R$ 3,3 milhões
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva declared R$ 4.8 million in assets to the TSE, a 35.7% decrease from R$ 7.4 million in 2022, mainly due to reduced VGBL holdings. Vice President Geraldo Alckmin declared R$ 3.3 million, a 227.3% increase from R$ 1 million in 2022. Together, their assets totaled R$ 8.1 million, down from R$ 8.4 million in the previous election.

item.title: Janja cutuca improvisos em discursos: "Acho que está virando tradição"
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva joked about being called to give an impromptu speech for the second time at an event involving President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, during the 30th anniversary celebration of the MTST in Taboão da Serra. She remarked that 'I think it’s becoming a tradition', referencing a similar occurrence at the PT’s national convention. Janja was announced after the presenter corrected an initial call for Minister Guilherme Boulos.

item.title: Lula registra candidatura à reeleição no TSE e declara patrimônio de R$ 4,7 milhões
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva filed his re-election candidacy for 2026, declaring assets of R$ 4.7 million — a 35.7% decrease from the R$ 7.4 million reported in 2022, mainly due to reduced private pension plan holdings. He also submitted an 84-page government plan proposing the creation of a Public Security Ministry, maintenance of the new fiscal framework, expansion of the Minha Casa Minha Vida housing program, and a goal of zero deforestation by 2030.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro miram voto feminino em discursos em SP; presidente critica Faria Lima
item.description: President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro held events in São Paulo on Saturday, targeting female voters ahead of the 2026 presidential election. Lula criticized the financial sector of Faria Lima, and both figures used electorally tinged agendas, although the official campaign period begins on August 16.

item.title: Governo espera reaproximação de Lula e Alcolumbre para destravar pauta
item.description: The Lula government hopes a forthcoming meeting between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre will improve dialogue and help unblock stalled priority agendas in the Senate, particularly the PEC to end the 6×1 work scale and the Public Security PEC. Although their recent dinner, mediated by STF ministers, signaled a thaw in relations, there are no guarantees these proposals will advance before the 2026 elections due to congressional slowdown in election years. Their rift began in April when the Senate rejected Lula’s nominee to the Supreme Court, with Alcolumbre playing a key role in the opposition.

item.title: Flávio critica Moraes: “Querem tirar até o direito de um pai abraçar seus filhos”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) criticized a decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes that denied a request for him and his brothers Carlos and Jair Renan to visit their father, Jair Bolsonaro, on Father's Day. In a post on X, Flávio claimed the ruling seeks to take away even a father's right to hug his children, accusing Moraes of overreach.

item.title: Lula foca em soberania, propõe mudar emendas e defende fim de 6×1 em plano de governo
item.description: The Lula-Alckmin ticket filed the first version of their government program, emphasizing democracy, national sovereignty, and reducing inequality. The 84-page document proposes expanding social policies, protecting women, strengthening public security through integrated forces and intelligence, combating organized crime, and criticizing parliamentary amendments while advocating for political reform.

item.title: Lula declara patrimônio 35% menor que em 2022
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) declared a net worth of R$ 4.7 million to Electoral Justice for the 2026 re-election bid, 35% lower than the R$ 7.4 million reported in 2022. The main decline occurred in private pension plans (VGBL), which total R$ 3.3 million this year. The decrease reflects adjustments in the composition of assets declared by the incumbent candidate.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reage após Moraes proibir visita de Dia dos Pais a Jair
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes after the denial of Father's Day visit permission to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, due to judicial rule violations. The family's defense argued the request was strictly humanitarian and exceptional, aiming to preserve family bonds. Moraes' decision followed the July dissemination of a letter written by Jair Bolsonaro, despite the ban on social media use.

item.title: Lula quer mostrar a Trump números de queda do desmatamento na Amazônia
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced he will send recent data from Brazil's space agency (Inpe) to U.S. President Donald Trump, showing a 36.87% drop in Amazon deforestation between August 2025 and July 2026 — the lowest level since 2016. Lula aims to counter the U.S. justification for imposing tariffs on Brazil, which cited illegal deforestation, by proving the official data reflects significant progress. He described the move as a response to misinformation that influenced the U.S. tariff decision.

item.title: PCO lança Rui Costa Pimenta Rui Costa Pimenta como candidato à Presidência em evento em SP
item.description: The Workers' Cause Party (PCO) launched Rui Costa Pimenta as its presidential candidate for the 2026 elections, with Antônio Carlos Silva as vice-presidential running mate. The ticket was unanimously approved at a national convention and frames itself as antissistema, rejecting electoral illusions and calling for revolutionary popular mobilization. Pimenta, running for president for the fifth time, also emphasized the Palestinian cause and denounced imperialism and workers' subordination to big capital.

item.title: Ex-ministro de Bolsonaro afirma que foi condenado por crime que não existia
item.description: Former Minister Anderson Torres, sentenced to 24 years for attempted coup and related acts tied to the January 8 attacks, filed a criminal review petition at the STF, claiming he was punished for crimes that did not exist at the time of the facts. His defense argues that the penal types for violent abolition of the Democratic Rule of Law and coup d'état were only incorporated into Brazilian law via Law No. 14,197/2021, which took effect in September 2021 — after the events leading to his conviction, including a presidential live in July 2021 and the seizure of a coup draft decree. The lawyers request his immediate release on provisional grounds, invoking the principle of legality and the non-retroactivity of harsher criminal law.

item.title: Patrimônio de Lula diminui 35%, com gasto de R$ 2,2 mi da aposentadoria
item.description: The personal wealth of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva decreased by 35% over his four-year term, dropping from R$ 7.42 million to R$ 4.78 million, according to the asset declaration submitted to the TSE. The decline was mainly due to R$ 2.2 million in expenditures from his pension.

item.title: Oposição usará pagamento a Marcola para vincular Lula ao PCC
item.description: Opposition supporters, led by Flávio Bolsonaro's allies, are attempting to link President Lula to the PCC by exploiting the nickname 'Marcola' of his former chief of staff, Marco Aurélio Santana, and a 249,000-real loan from Roberta Luchinger, a friend of Lulinha. The narrative gained traction after the U.S. designated PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, which Bolsonaro uses to accuse Lula of being 'the PCC's chief,' claiming the president opposes national security interests.

item.title: Em igreja, Caiado reforça elo com evangélicos: "De longo tempo"
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, presidential candidate from the PSD party, strengthened his ties with evangelical voters during a meeting with Assemblies of God leaders in São Paulo. He emphasized that his relationship with the evangelical bloc — representing about 30% of the Brazilian electorate — has been long-standing and crucial for governability, citing social actions and pandemic-era support. Caiado’s evangelical outreach has raised alarms in Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign, which also relies heavily on this voter base.

item.title: Lula admite baixa adesão a programa para trabalhadores de aplicativo e acusa bancos de segurarem empréstimos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva admitted that the Move Brasil program, designed to finance vehicles for app-based workers, is experiencing lower-than-expected uptake due to stringent bank requirements such as credit checks and income verification. He blamed banks for blocking financing and said he had held meetings to pressure Caixa Econômica Federal and Banco do Brasil, including sending Minister Guilherme Boulos to mobilize workers who were denied access to the program.

item.title: Lula: nenhum banqueiro da Faria Lima ou ruralista sabe o que é acordar com rato nadando em casa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized Faria Lima bankers and ruralists for not understanding the reality of floods and the daily struggles of poor people, saying they don’t know what it’s like to wake up with a rat swimming in their home. He argued that those who set interest rates and defend fiscal adjustment are disconnected from how ordinary Brazilians live.

item.title: Dois retratos revelam o paradoxo da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro announced Alfredo Gaspar as his running mate in a sparsely attended event, underscoring his weakness in party alliance-building, as he failed to secure support from Centrão-aligned parties. Nevertheless, recent polls show a narrowing gap with Lula, with Bolsonaro gaining traction among independent voters, preserving his competitiveness despite lacking formal party backing.

item.title: Flávio acena ao eleitorado feminino e fala em indicar mulheres ao STF
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) reached out to female voters in Itapetininga, promising to appoint both men and women to the Supreme Federal Court if elected. He emphasized gender balance on the Court as part of his 2026 campaign strategy to gain support among women.

item.title: Flávio critica contas de Lula e promete Brasil entre as 7 maiores economias
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL party's presidential candidate, criticized Lula's government indebtedness and pledged to balance public accounts, restore investor confidence, and bring Brazil into the world's top seven economies by the end of his potential term. He denounced the 'leftist mindset' as a 'cancer of Brazil' and called the election decisive for the nation's future, while also proposing policies to support women entrepreneurs, including expanding microcredit access and doubling the number of female business owners.

item.title: Lula declara R$ 4,7 milhões em patrimônio ao TSE, valor 35% menor em relação a 2022
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva declared R$ 4.7 million in assets to the TSE for the 2026 elections, a 35% decrease from R$ 7.4 million in 2022. The bulk of his wealth is in private pension plans (R$ 3.3 million), followed by real estate (R$ 739,200) and financial investments (R$ 454,200). The decline is primarily due to a R$ 2.7 million reduction in VGBL pension plans.

item.title: Em evento do MTST, Lula critica Faria Lima e cobranças por ajuste fiscal e pressiona por fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Lula criticized interest rates and market demands for fiscal adjustment, accusing elites of not understanding the reality of the poor. Speaking at an MTST event in Taboão da Serra, he urged the public to study Brazilian presidential history to recognize his commitment to social inclusion, while Boulos highlighted Minha Casa, Minha Vida projects and attacked Bolsonaro for ending the program.

item.title: Flávio critica decisão de Moraes que barrou visita a Bolsonaro no Dia dos Pais
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to block a visit by his brothers Carlos and Jair Renan to their father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, on Father's Day, claiming it deprives a father of the right to embrace his children. The ruling upholds a 30-day suspension of visits, allowing only medical, physiotherapeutic, and legal meetings, following Bolsonaro's breach of court-imposed conditions, including Flávio's social media publication of a letter from the former president.

item.title: SEM ALTERNATIVAS, ESQUERDA registra MAIS uma CANDIDATURA do LULA
item.description: The Brazilian left is struggling to find alternatives to former president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who is expected to run again in 2026, as indicated by recent campaign materials. Despite the possibility of a uncontested candidacy, there are signs of internal mobilization to consolidate his name as a viable option amid the lack of other competitive figures in the progressive camp.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro fala em indicar mulheres ao STF em evento com aliadas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL party's presidential candidate, again criticized Supreme Court (STF) ministers during a campaign event in the interior of São Paulo. Seeking to appeal to female voters, he stated that, if elected, he would appoint 'men and women' to the Court, combining his conservative agenda with an effort to broaden support among women.

item.title: “Moraes nega visita a Bolsonaro no Dia dos Pais”
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes rejected Jair Bolsonaro's request to receive his children on Father's Day, upholding the suspension of all visits except for medical and legal teams. The decision stems from Bolsonaro's violation of house arrest conditions after his son Flávio published a handwritten letter from him on social media, breaching the ban on digital platform access.
